Enki.fact: She raises an army and takes the god Qingu as her new consort.

Enki.fact: When Ea learns of her preparations, he is horrified and brings the news to his grandfather Anshar. Anshar is initially angered and blames Ea for the situation caused by his murder of Abzû.

Enki.fact: Anshar then orders Ea to defeat Tiamat. Ea then summons his son and instructs him to seek out Anshar and volunteer to challenge Tiamat.

Enki.fact: Anshar is initially angered and blames Ea for the situation caused by his murder of Abzû. Anshar then orders Ea to defeat Tiamat.

Enki.fact: Anshar then orders Ea to defeat Tiamat. He fails, and Anshar then sends Anu, who also fails.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: Ea then summons his son and instructs him to seek out Anshar and volunteer to challenge Tiamat. After his defeat of Tiamat, Marduk organizes the universe.

Enki.fact: The rebellious gods single out Qingu.

Enki.fact: In the last sections dealing with Marduk's multiples names, Ea gives to his son his own name, and puts him in charge of his offices.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: They set fire to their tools and surround Enlil's Ekur shrine in Nippur.

Enki.fact: Enlil is woken up by his vizier Nusku, who informs him of the situation.

Enki.fact: In the next section of the myth, mankind has multiplied, and they create so much noise that Enlil is unable to sleep.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Humans multiply, and once again _____ is unable to sleep due to the noise
Enki.fact: Humans multiply, and once again Enlil is unable to sleep due to the noise.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He decides this time to wipe out humanity with a famine and orders _____, the weather-god, to withhold his rain
Enki.fact: He decides this time to wipe out humanity with a famine and orders Adad, the weather-god, to withhold his rain. Once more Atra-ḫasīs prays to Enki, who instructs him to tell his fellow men to stop praying and sending offerings to all of the gods, and to instead concentrate their offerings on Adad.

Enki.fact: Atra-ḫasīs speaks with his elders and explains his departure by telling them that since Enki had a falling out with Enlil, he, as Enki's servant, must leave Enlil's earth. On the seventh day the flood comes and wipes out humanity, with the exception of Atra-ḫasīs and his family on the boat.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: On the seventh day the flood comes and wipes out humanity, with the exception of Atra-ḫasīs and his family on the boat. When the flood ends, Atra-ḫasīs makes an offering to the gods.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: As the oldest fragment preserving this myth dates from around the same period as the tablets preserving Atra-ḫasīs, the relation between the two texts is uncertain.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: The flood story in the Epic of Gilgamesh is believed to be based on the one in Atra-ḫasīs. Gilgamesh meets the flood survivor, here named Utnapishtim, during his quest for immortality.

Enki.question: Gilgamesh meets the flood survivor, here named _____, during his quest for immortality
Enki.fact: Gilgamesh meets the flood survivor, here named Utnapishtim, during his quest for immortality. Utnapishtim tells him how he and his wife survived the flood and were made immortal by the gods as a result.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: Utnapishtim tells him how he and his wife survived the flood and were made immortal by the gods as a result. Ea, who did not wish to see mankind destroyed, found a way around his oath and warned Utnapishtim.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: With the help of his people, _____ built a massive boat that he filled with his kin, possessions, and animals
Enki.fact: Ea, who did not wish to see mankind destroyed, found a way around his oath and warned Utnapishtim. When Utnapishtim asked him what to tell the elders and the people of his city of Shuruppak, Ea instructed him to tell them that since he had fallen out with Enlil, he could not remain on the earth and that he was going to live in Ea's underground ocean.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: When the flood stopped, _____ sent three birds to see if the waters had decreased enough for him to land
Enki.fact: With the help of his people, Utnapishtim built a massive boat that he filled with his kin, possessions, and animals. When the flood stopped, Utnapishtim sent three birds to see if the waters had decreased enough for him to land.

Enki.fact: This episode has been compared to a similar one in the account of the flood related in the Book of Genesis.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: When the flood stopped, Utnapishtim sent three birds to see if the waters had decreased enough for him to land. After the last bird failed to come back to the boat, Utnapishtim prepared an offering for the gods on the top of the mountain.

Enki.fact: When Enlil realized that humans still lived, he was furious, and demanded to know the reason for their survival. Ea told Enlil that his decision to wipe out humanity was a disproportionate punishment, and proposed other ways to control the size of its population.

Enki.fact: Enlil, convinced to let humanity live, granted Utnapishtim and his wife immortality.

Enki.fact: Berossos transmitted a variant of the Mesopotamian story of the flood in his Babyloniaca, a work meant to present the history of the Babylonians to the Greeks.

Enki.fact: His original work is lost, but it is known from quotes of Alexander Polyhistor and Abydenus, themselves quoted by Eusebius.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: There Kronos warns Xisuthros (the hellenized form of the sumerian Ziusudra) about the incoming flood, appearing to him in a dream in the version quoted by Polyhistor.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: He tells him the exact month in which the flood will come, and also instructs him to bury all writings in Sippar, two details which are not present in the older cuneiform sources.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Inanna takes them and loads them into the Boat of _____, and she departs for her city of Uruk
Enki.fact: Inanna takes them and loads them into the Boat of Heaven, and she departs for her city of Uruk. Enki's reaction is missing due to the fragmentary of the text at this point, but determined to get back the me-s, he dispatches Isimud and enkum servants to seize the Boat of Heaven and its cargo.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He asks _____ where they are, and the sukkal replies that he has given them all to Inanna
Enki.fact: He asks Isimud where they are, and the sukkal replies that he has given them all to Inanna. Enki's reaction is missing due to the fragmentary of the text at this point, but determined to get back the me-s, he dispatches Isimud and enkum servants to seize the Boat of Heaven and its cargo.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: As soon as the enkums grab the Boat, Inanna summons her sukkal Ninshubur, who prevents them from seizing it in unclear circumstances. Each time, Inanna calls Ninshubur and the Boat of Heaven is able to continue its journey.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: As soon as the enkums grab the Boat, Inanna summons her sukkal Ninshubur, who prevents them from seizing it in unclear circumstances. Each time, Inanna calls Ninshubur and the Boat of Heaven is able to continue its journey.

Enki.fact: The second time, he dispatches Isimud alongside the fifty giants of Eridu, the third time alongside the fifty Lahamu of the Engur, the fourth time alongside the "Big fish", the fifth time alongside the guards of Uruk, and the sixth time alongside the guards of the Turungal canal. Inanna eventually reaches Uruk triumphantly and unloads the me-s among the celebration of her people.

Enki.fact: In the Sumerian version, as Inanna makes her preparations to journey into the Underworld, she instructs her sukkal Ninshubur to ask Enlil, Nanna, and Enki for help if something happens to her. The queen of the Underworld, Ereshkigal, is displeased to learn of Inanna's visit.

Enki.fact: The queen of the Underworld, Ereshkigal, is displeased to learn of Inanna's visit. When Inanna is brought into her presence, Ereshkigal strikes her down and hangs her corpse from a nail.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: In the Sumerian version, as Inanna makes her preparations to journey into the Underworld, she instructs her sukkal Ninshubur to ask Enlil, Nanna, and Enki for help if something happens to her. Ninshubur, in mourning, goes to see Enlil and Nanna, but both of them refuse to help her.

Enki.fact: Finally they are to sprinkle the food of life and the water of life upon it to revive Inanna. The plan succeeds, and Inanna is able to leave the Underworld, though she then has to find a substitute to take her place there.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: Ea creates Asushunamir, an androgynous figure, and instructs them to appease Ereshkigal, and then to have her swear an oath of the great gods to give them the water of life. Ishtar is revived, but Ereshkigal is furious and she curses Asushunamir to a grim life on earth.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ishtar is revived, but _____ is furious and she curses Asushunamir to a grim life on earth
Enki.fact: Ea creates Asushunamir, an androgynous figure, and instructs them to appease Ereshkigal, and then to have her swear an oath of the great gods to give them the water of life. Ishtar is revived, but Ereshkigal is furious and she curses Asushunamir to a grim life on earth.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Here the god appears in his usual role in _____ literature as an ingenious deity who devises plans to resolve difficult situations
Enki.fact: Here the god appears in his usual role in Mesopotamian literature as an ingenious deity who devises plans to resolve difficult situations.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: Ishtar is revived, but Ereshkigal is furious and she curses Asushunamir to a grim life on earth. The poem begins with a hymn praising Ishtar in her aspect as the goddess of war.

Enki.fact: Ea then tells Ṣaltu that she has been created to disrespectfully challenge Ishtar, whom he calls Irnina ( the name of one of her aspects) and he instructs her on how she is to act. He proceeds to describe Ishtar so that Ṣaltu might recognize her.

Enki.fact: An and Enlil are seated in the high place, and Nintu is seated at a place of honor. At the end of the composition, Enlil, pleased by the banquet, gives a blessing praising Enki's temple.

Enki.fact: Some scholars argue that lines 136–155 are not the evocation of the spell of Nudimmud, and that they are therefore not part of Enmerkar's speech.

Enki.fact: An unification of the languages, but taking place in the past, has also been proposed by Christoph Uehlinger.

Enki.fact: Under his advice, the gods summon Ninurta's mother Mami, cover her with honors, name her ''Mistress of all the gods'', Belet-ili, and name her son Ninurta champion of the gods. Enki.fact: Ninurta sends Sharur back to Ea to ask for help.

Enki.fact: Unhappy with his promises, Ninurta begins to secretly plot against Enki, who becomes aware of his plans. After Ninurta raises his hand against Enki's sukkal Isimud in an altercation, Enki fashions a turtle from the clay of the Abzû and stations it next to the gates of the Abzu.

Enki.fact: He lures Ninurta to this location, and pretends to be ignorant of the situation when he is attacked by the turtle. The turtle digs a pit and pushes Ninurta into it.

Enki.question: Ninmena is identified by _____ as a name of Ninhursag in this context
Enki.fact: Ninmena is identified by Kramer as a name of Ninhursag in this context. Kramer translates this epithet as "my plant-eater" and connects it to the myth Enki and Ninhursag.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: The mother of Ninurta, who appears here under the name Ninmena, comes to ask for her son's release. Ninmena is identified by Kramer as a name of Ninhursag in this context.

Enki.fact: The myth is known from two slightly different versions, a shorter one attested from a Middle Babylonian Manuscript, and a much longer one known from a seventh century source and one from Neo-Babylonian Uruk.

Enki.fact: While Nergal follows most of Ea's advice, he fails to follow the last one and has sex with Ereshkigal. On the seventh day, while Ereshkigal is asleep, Nergal leaves the Underworld.
